S1.user_text: Consider the electromagnetic field. Prepare the electric field $\mathbf E$ and magnetic field $\mathbf B$ as vector fields (components registered abstractly, to be assigned concrete expressions next).

S8.user_text: Assign the components of the electric field for a linearly polarized plane wave traveling in the $+x$ direction (amplitude 1, wavevector $k$, angular frequency $\omega$).

S15.user_text: Assign the corresponding components of the magnetic field.

S22.user_text: Compute the divergence of the electric field $\nabla\cdot\mathbf E$. In vacuum (no charge), this should vanish identically (Gauss's law).

S25.user_text: Compute the divergence of the magnetic field $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$. Since no magnetic charge exists, this should vanish identically.

S28.user_text: Compute the curl of the electric field $\nabla\times\mathbf E$ (the left-hand side of Faraday's law).

S31.user_text: Compute the curl of the magnetic field $\nabla\times\mathbf B$ (the left-hand side of Ampere's law).

S34.user_text: Since $\partial/\partial t$ cannot act directly on a vector field, take the time derivative component by component. Here, take the partial derivative of the nonzero component $B_z$ with respect to $t$.

S35.user_text: Take the partial derivative of B_z with respect to t

S37.user_text: Assemble the derivative just found into a new vector field, which we name `dBdt` — a plain identifier chosen here to stand for $d\mathbf B/dt$ (it is not a CAS keyword or special syntax; any other name would work identically), assigning each component in turn.

S47.user_text: Confirm that the assembled $d\mathbf B/dt$ can be used in further calculations (such as a divergence) by computing its divergence.

S50.user_text: Register the $z$-components of Faraday's law $\nabla\times\mathbf E=-\partial\mathbf B/\partial t$ as an equality (comparing the $z$-component of each side).

S53.user_text: Solve this equality for the angular frequency $\omega$ to obtain the consistency condition (dispersion relation) $\omega=ck$.

S55.rendered_command: solve(-k * sin(k * x - w * t)=-w * sin(k * x - w * t) * c^-1, w)
